description: eSPIRS is the European Commission's register of establishments that fall under the Seveso Directive on the control of major-accident hazards involving dangerous substances, maintained by the Joint Research Centre's Major Accident Hazards Bureau from the information EU member states report. Its purpose is to hold the establishments covered by the Seveso Directive that countries report, so that major-hazard sites can be located and compared; the fields could not be read without a login. Coverage is the EU and participating countries, per establishment. On 26 September 2026 the entry page stated that access to eSPIRS and eMARS requires EU Login with two-factor authentication, and that users see the tools according to their authorisation level. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY-4.0 (European Commission reuse policy: EU-owned content under CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise noted). Access is free of charge. Caveats: detailed site data are restricted to authorised authority users for security reasons, public content is limited, and the login requirement prevents scripted harvesting. For simulation it gives the locations and hazard classes of major chemical and industrial sites for natech, hazard exposure and land-use planning studies around transport, energy and residential infrastructure. Related catalogue records include eMARS, the European Industrial Emissions Portal and the EPA Facility Registry Service.
